rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: The responsible person must carry out and regularly review a fire risk assessment of the premises.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: A written record of the fire risk assessment must be kept.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: The assessment process includes identifying fire hazards and identifying people at risk.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: The responsible person must evaluate, remove or reduce fire risks.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: Findings should be recorded and supported by an emergency plan and training.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: The assessment should consider emergency routes and exits and fire detection and warning systems.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: The assessment should consider firefighting equipment and safe storage or removal of dangerous substances.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: Emergency planning should consider vulnerable people and provide information to employees and other people on the premises.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: Fire controls depend on premises use, occupancy, vulnerable people, processes, layout, ignition sources and available evacuation routes.

rows.source: GOV.UK workplace fire safety
rows.verified: Workplace-fire evidence is premises- and activity-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: People and organisations can check for flooding expected in the next five days.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: The Environment Agency provides flood warnings by text, phone or email for eligible locations in England.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: Long-term flood risk can be checked for rivers, the sea, surface water, reservoirs and groundwater where data is available.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: Households, communities and businesses can prepare a flood plan before an incident.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: Flood plans should keep essential medication, important documents and contact details accessible.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: A flood alert means flooding is possible and people should prepare.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: A flood warning means flooding is expected and people should take action.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: The flood-warning registration service does not provide warnings for surface-water flash flooding.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: Flood actions depend on warning type, source, location, forecast, property vulnerability, access routes and available support.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood preparedness and warnings
rows.verified: Flood-warning evidence is location- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level flood probability.
